(PER: THE HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE J.M.KHAZI) Appellant who is the sole accused has filed this appeal under Section 14A(2) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities)
Act, 2015 ('the Act' for short), seeking regular bail for the offences punishable under Section 376(2(n), 376(3), 363 of IPC r/w Section 4(2) and 6 of POCSO Act, and under Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act, 2015.

sentences.text: 2. In support of the appeal, the appellant contended that the complaint averments falsify the allegations that prosecutrix was kidnapped by the appellant.
The investigating officer has failed to collect the birth certificate of the prosecutrix to prove her age.

The allegations that the appellant kidnapped the prosecutrix and took her to Gajendragad and from there to Goa and later, they returned to Bangalore and stayed in a room till NC: 2024:KHC-D:18105 18.05.2024 falsifies the allegation that she was kidnapped by the appellant.
The appellant is falsely implicated.
He was arrested on 18.05.2024 and since then he is in judicial custody.
Already investigation is completed and charge sheet is filed.
Appellant is ready and willing to abide by any conditions that may be imposed and offer substantial sureties to the satisfaction of the trial Court and hence, the appeal.
3. Learned HCGP submitted oral objections stating that as on the date of incident prosecutrix was aged 16 years.
On 02.05.2024, at 8.00 am, complainant left the house to work in the land.
At 12.00 noon, when he returned home, his wife disclosed that prosecutrix has left the house to go the tailoring shop of one Bajanri, but, has not returned.
Both of them searched for her everywhere and filed the complaint.
They suspect that someone might have kidnapped her.
3.1. Based on the said complaint, case is registered against unknown person and investigation is taken up.
The petitioner and prosecutrix were secured from Bengaluru NC: 2024:KHC-D:18105 and subjected to medical examination.

The statement of the prosecutrix revealed that since from 1 year,
the petitioner was after her.
They were in love.
Though they belong to different caste and the prosecutrix was still minor.
The petitioner was intending to marry her.
On 19.02.2024, the petitioner forcibly took her inside the house and had sexual intercourse.
She did not disclose this fact to her parents fearing that they may stop her going to the school.
3.2. On 02.05.2024, at 11.00 a.m., on the instructions of the petitioner, she left the house in the pretext of going to tailor's house/shop

At 11.30 a.m., prosecutrix left her village in an auto rickshaw Basavaraj S/O Sharanappa Gudi vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125265218/
2 and went to Gajendragad and petitioner was there.

sentences.text: Both of them travelled to Goa in bus.
After spending two days at Goa, on 05.05.2024 they came to Bengaluru and stayed in a room at Jumbo Savari area till 18.05.2024.
During this period, the petitioner had sexually intercourse with her.
3.3. On 18.05.2024 her parents and Police Officials came to Bengaluru and brought her to Hanumasagar NC: 2024:KHC-D:18105 Police Station.
The statement of the prosecutrix is also recorded before the learned Magistrate under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C.
After conducting detailed investigation, charge sheet is filed against the petitioner.
It makes out a strong prima facie case.
The allegations made against the petitioner are very grave.
In the event of granting bail, petitioner may threaten or tamper with witnesses.
He may also abscond and thereby by delay and defeat the proceedings and pray to reject the petition.

4. Heard the arguments and perused the records.
5.
As per the complaint averments, at the time of incident, the prosecutrix was aged 16 years.

It is alleged that since 1 year prior to the date of incident, the petitioner was expressing his love to the prosecutrix and about 4 months prior to the filing of the complaint, he had sexually intercourse with her in his house.
The statement of the prosecutrix reveal that on 02.05.2024, she left her house under the pretext of visiting the tailor and went to Gajendragad bus stand in an auto rickshaw.
From there, both of them went to Goa in bus and after spending two NC: 2024:KHC-D:18105 days, they went to Bengaluru and stayed in a room till 18.05.2024.
It is alleged that during this period, the prosecutrix was sexually assaulted by the petitioner.
6. After the petitioner and prosecutrix were secured by the Police, they are subjected to medical examination.
The FSL report is awaited.
After conducting detailed investigation, the concerned Police have filed charge sheet.
The petitioner was arrested on 20.05.2024 and since then, he is in judicial custody.

Since investigation is completed and charge sheet is filed, no longer is custodial presence of the petitioner required for the purpose of investigation and therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that petitioner is entitled for bail.
However, there is apprehension that in the event of granting bail, petitioner may threaten or tamper with the witnesses.
He may also abscond and thereby delayed the trial.

However, suitable conditions may be imposed to overcome the apprehension of the prosecution and accordingly, the following:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:18105 ORDER i.
Appeal filed by accused/appellant is hereby allowed.
ii. The impugned order dated 20.08.2024  passed by the Additional District and  Sessions Judge, FTSC-1 at Koppal in Hanumasagar P.S. Crime No.60/2024 is set aside.
